The Firefly 220R is the same lantern as the Firefly 220 with the battery compartment replaced by a
sealed 2,600 mAh lithium-ion pack. It is the same size, gives the same 220 lumens from the same
globe, and uses the same two brightness levels, but it charges from any USB-C source in 3.5 hours
and never needs cells. The extra 30 grams are the battery. A USB-A port under a rubber flap lets
it charge a phone in an emergency; the port supplies 5 volts at 1 amp, enough to top up a phone
but not to charge a tablet. The battery is not user-replaceable and is covered for 1 year, while
the rest of the lantern carries the standard 2-year warranty. Four blue LEDs beside the USB-C port
show the state of charge.

The Beacon 600 is our camp lantern: big enough to light a four-person tent or a picnic shelter,
heavy enough to stay put in wind. Four D cells last five nights of evening use on high, and on low
the lantern runs for five days straight. The red night mode keeps night vision while you find your
way to the car. A steel hanging hook screws into the top, and the shoulder strap clips to the bail.
The globe is glass, which gives a cleaner light than polycarbonate but can break; a replacement
globe is part G-600 and fits in two minutes with no tools. Batteries are not included because D
cells ship badly and most customers have a preference.

Compatible parts: globe G-600, hanging hook H-600, shoulder strap S-600.

### Changes

- Wishlists, with sharing by link.
- Canada as a shipping destination; address forms accept provinces and postal codes.
- Product compare for up to three products.
- The product page shows the model number under the product name, since customers ordering

### Fixes

- The Firefly 220R product page showed the Firefly 220's runtime (42 hours on low) instead of
  its own (48 hours on low). The two products share a page template and the runtime field was
  pointing at the wrong product record. Customers who bought a 220R between May 19 and August
  11 and asked about the difference were offered a 40-day return by Customer Service.
- Order lookup rejected order numbers typed in lower case.
- The holiday return extension banner was showing in July.

### Known issues

- Compare does not include discontinued products, so a Beacon 400 owner cannot compare it to
  the Beacon 600.

Hagerstown Kerosene Lantern (LS-HK12)
The Hagerstown is a plain 12-inch hurricane lantern and there is not much to go wrong with
it. It burns K-1 kerosene or Clearburn lamp oil and uses a #2 flat wick, part W-78, sold in a
5-pack. Faults are a smoky flame (wick), a flame that will not stay lit (wick or air tubes), and
a tank that weeps at the seam (replace the lantern; we do not repair tanks).
Wick trimming and replacement
1. Raise the globe with the lever and lift the burner cone off.
2. Wind the wick up 10 mm. Trim it straight across with the wick scissors, then take the
two corners off at 45 degrees. A square-cut wick smokes at the corners.
3. If the wick is charred for more than 25 mm, or is less than 100 mm long, replace it.
Feed the new W-78 down through the burner with the raised side toward the winder
knob.
4. Soak a new wick in lamp oil for 10 minutes before lighting it.

5. Light under the hood and set the flame so that it is just below the point where it
smokes. Run the 30-minute burn-in.
Air tubes and burner
The two side tubes carry air to the burner. If they are dented so that a 4 mm rod will not
pass, straighten them with the tube mandrel or replace the lantern. The burner itself (part
BR-12) is replaced only when the winder gear strips, which happens about twice a year
across the whole fleet.
Firefly 220 and 220R
The Firefly 220 (LS-220) runs on three AA cells; the Firefly 220R (LS-220R) is the
rechargeable model with the 2,600 mAh pack and a USB-C port. They look the same from
the outside except for the port cover, and the 220R weighs 30 g more. Check the model
number on the base plate before you order parts: the switches are different and the 220's
switch will not fit the 220R.
Switch
1. Remove the base (two Phillips screws on the 220, three on the 220R).
2. The switch is a tactile switch on the main board. Switch part numbers: SW-220 for the
220, SW-220R for the 220R. Both are soldered; this is the one soldering job on the
Firefly bench.
3. Replace the switch, refit, and check both brightness levels.
Firefly 220R USB-C port

Firefly 220R USB-C port
A 220R that will not charge is usually the cable, then the port, then the pack, in that order.
Test with the bench cable (part C-15) before opening anything.
1. Open the base (three screws) and lift out the pack. Pack part is B-220R.
2. The port is part of the main board (PCB-220R); the board is replaced as a unit, $9.00
on a paid repair.
3. On refit, check the port cover seals; the 220R is IPX4 and the cover is part of that
rating.
4. Charge to full on the bench (about 3.5 hours) and check the power bank output with
the load tester: it should hold 5 V at 1 A for 10 minutes.

[4] faq.md > What is the difference between the Firefly 220 and the Firefly 220R?
## Products

### What is the difference between the Firefly 220 and the Firefly 220R?

They are the same size and give the same 220 lumens. The Firefly 220 ($34.99) runs on three AA
batteries, which are included, for 42 hours on low or 9 hours on high. The Firefly 220R ($54.99)
has a built-in 2,600 mAh rechargeable battery that charges over USB-C, runs 48 hours on low or 10
hours on high, and can charge a phone from its USB-A port. The 220R weighs 30 grams more.

### How long does the Firefly 220R take to charge?

About 3.5 hours from empty with a 5 volt 2 amp USB charger. Four blue lights beside the port show
how full the battery is.
